summary: Thubten Samphel was a Tibetologist who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and Columbia University (~1980–1982). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.

Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, Zongkar Choede Monastery, and Cambridge, and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, where he became chief editor around 1999.

Théodore Pavie was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Thích Minh Châu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (~1957–1961). He lectured at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1961) and served as Vice Chancellor of Van Hanh University (~1964–1975).

Thích Thiện Châu was a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued higher education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University and completing a doctoral dissertation at Sorbonne Nouvelle University by 1977.

Tianshu Zhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Northwest University and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, and has held academic posts at Northwest University, Ohio State, Shaanxi History Museum, and Korea University.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a Buddhist studies scholar who headed the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and served as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, and became a professor at Leiden University in 1974, succeeding David Seyfort Ruegg.
Timothy Asch was an academic who completed his education at The Putney School, Columbia University (~1955–1959), Boston University, and Harvard University.

Timothy H. Barrett is a scholar in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Cambridge and Yale. He taught at the University of Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy J. Dean studied under Robert Clark at the University of East Anglia, later attending Brandeis and Johns Hopkins. He was a fellow at Stanford (1997–1998) and held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox at the University of Washington, where he subsequently held faculty posts (attested 1998–2026).
Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1994. He holds an academic post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).

Tirumalai Krishnamacharya was an Indology scholar who studied under Ramamohana Brahmachari, Shivakumar Shastry, and others at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Mysore. He taught at Maharaja's Sanskrit College, Mysore (1931) and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College.

Tiruvengadu Narayanayajwa Ramachandran was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (attested 1933) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi.

Tissa Rajapatirana is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD (1966–1974) at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He subsequently held a post at ANU's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).

Tista Biswas is an Indologist who studied under doctoral supervisor Subuddhi Charan Goswami and holds the post of Sir William Jones Research Fellow in Sanskritic Studies at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).
Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, where he completed his PhD under the supervision of György Kara (attested 1991).

Todd Thornton Lewis is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology who studied at Columbia University. He has held academic appointments at the College of the Holy Cross, including a distinguished professorship (attested 1996, 2016–2017).
